title: Prescribed root generators and their signed scalar normalization
statement: Fix a finite-field datum, a prime different from its characteristic, and a section at the final object of the Tate sheaf $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$ [def-pur-twist-sheaves] whose projections to the roots-of-unity tower [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], read as root values, are primitive at every positive prime-power level [def-pur-point-tate-comparison-data]. There are integral section generators g for every finite coefficient field and signed degree: g in nonnegative degree is precisely positiveGenerator, its negative generator evaluates to one on the corresponding prescribed positive generator, finite signed reduction of every nonnegative generator is the finite Tate power generator finiteTateProPowerGenerator of the same root section [def-amb-finite-tate-site-comparison-data], and every canonical signed scalar map carries g to g at the target coefficient field. All maps and generators are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] [lem-weil-signed-twist-reduction-comparison].

proof.text: define the root tuple by evaluating the given section at each tower level. The limit equations imply compatibility of successive roots. Apply point_tate_root_coordinates at every coefficient field with this tuple. Its normalized completed basis has image of one equal to the given section: project to every root level, use its root formula on one, and use injectivity of Spec's section identification, then the universal property of the inverse limit. The integral coordinate in degree one is therefore the prescribed root tensor. Tensor recursion identifies every nonnegative coordinate with positiveGenerator, including the coefficient unit in degree zero. In negative degree take the dual coordinate; its evaluation on the corresponding positive generator is one. The final section clause of root coordinates makes a ↦ a times this generator bijective. For finite reduction, use the zero and degree-one formulas of signedTwistReduction_comparison and induct on tensor powers. For scalar extension, the root tensor formula and tensor recursion preserve the positive generators. The normalized evaluation formula preserves negative generators as well, since on the target positive basis a functional is determined by its value on one. All generators in this argument use the same initial root section.

theorem normalizedSectionGenerators (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (e : (purTwistZlOne (Spec (.of D.k)) l).obj.obj (finalObject D))
    (he : ∀ r : ℕ, IsPrimitiveRoot
      (rootValue D (l ^ (r + 1))
        ((limit.π (proEtaleRootsOfUnityTower (Spec (.of D.k)) l Fact.out) (op r)).hom.app
          (finalObject D) e)) (l ^ (r + 1))) :
    ∃ (g : ∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (m : ℤ), integral D l F m),
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (r : ℕ),
      g F (r : ℤ) = positiveGenerator D l F e r) ∧
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (r : ℕ),
      integralEvaluate D l F r (g F (Int.negSucc r))
        (positiveGenerator D l F e (r + 1)) = 1) ∧
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (n r : ℕ),
      (reduction D l F hl n (r : ℤ)).val.app (finalObject D) (g F (r : ℤ)) =
        finiteTateProPowerGenerator l F n (Spec (.of D.k)) (finalObject D) 1 r
          (fun _ ↦ e)) ∧
    (∀ (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Padic l) L]
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) L] (ι : F →ₐ[Padic l] L) (m : ℤ),
      (scalarMap D l F hl L ι m).val.app (finalObject D) (g F m) = g L m)
